summary: Iteration 9 — post-corruption rebuild + Emergent Google Auth + owner-approver / 3-member team model verified end-to-end. Backend: 26 new auth/team/approval tests (test_auth_and_approvals.py) all PASS in 3.9s AND all 56 pre-corruption regression tests still PASS in 29.7s after the shared session fixture in backend_test.py was updated to send `Authorization: Bearer tok_owner_e2e` (auth-gating is applied to every /api path except OPEN_PATHS). Total 82/82 backend tests green. Frontend: unauth home shows login-page + google-login-btn (dashboard NOT leaked); /spin?space=Test loads publicly and can spin without auth; owner cookie session_token=tok_owner_e2e unlocks dashboard with user-card 'Test Owner · Owner · Approver', nav-team, logout-btn, and all 4 modules (Command Center / Executioner / Maximizer / Content Director) render cleanly with real data ($4,547.15 revenue, 5.48x ROAS, calendar, brand brain, distribution). Team & Approvals page renders access-code-card (TR-XXXX-XXXX), copy-code-btn, rotate-code-btn -> confirm-rotate-btn -> new code + old locked out (verified: TR-T4FY-KYS4 -> TR-RZWE-JF9K), members-card with seats-used (0/3 -> 1/3 after activation), approvals-card. Seeded a fresh pending member (test-fresh-member), verified ActivateGate renders (activate-gate, access-code-input, access-code-submit, access-code-error), wrong code -> 400 with visible error, correct code unlocks dashboard, member's Publish-All click -> toast 'Sent to owner for approval' + 'Submitted to the account owner for approval'. Owner side: nav-pending-badge shows '1', Team page shows approval-{id} with approve-{id}/reject-{id}; clicking approve executed the publish (toast 'Approved & executed — Published to 3 surfaces') and moved item to history-{id} with 'Approved' badge; approvals-card returned to 'no-pending' empty state. Rotate-code locked out the active fresh member as expected (row showed 'Locked Out'). Logout-btn kills the server-side session AND redirects to login page (verified /api/auth/me returns 401 after). All required data-testids present and working. One minor UX bug: copy-code-btn does not catch clipboard promise rejection (uncaught NotAllowedError overlay in headless/no-permission contexts).

ui_bugs.issue: navigator.clipboard.writeText() rejection is not caught. In contexts where clipboard permission is denied (Playwright headless, private windows, older Safari, permissions-policy off) the app surfaces an uncaught runtime error overlay. Wrap the call in try/catch and fall back to a `document.execCommand('copy')` on a hidden textarea, and show a sonner toast 'Copied' vs 'Copy blocked — select and copy manually'.

action_items: LOW: Team.js — wrap navigator.clipboard.writeText call in try/catch (see frontend_issues above). Not a blocker; only visible in clipboard-denied contexts.
OPTIONAL (from prior iters, still valid): server.py ~2000 lines — split into routers/services. auth.py is fine as-is.

OPTIONAL: rotate-code endpoint has NO confirmation step at the API layer (only in UI); if the endpoint is ever called by CSRF or a rogue script the code rotates silently. Consider requiring `{confirm: true}` body param.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py get_session_user() reads session_token from cookie OR Authorization header — good. But there's no rotation of tokens on activate/rotate, so a leaked session lives its full 7 days. Consider bumping session token on privileged actions.

auth.py revoke_member deletes all sessions immediately (great) but restore_member only sets status=pending; the member has NO session so they must sign in again (as documented) — expected but worth noting in the UI toast.
submit_or_execute stores full payload inside db.approvals — for a real publish-all with a large asset attachment this could bloat mongodb. Consider storing a payload_ref -> S3 URI instead.

auth.py OPEN_PATHS is a set of exact strings; if a future route like /api/maximizer/spin/qr becomes public it must be added explicitly. This is a good default (deny-by-default) but flag for maintenance.

Frontend AuthContext presumably polls /api/auth/me on interval — verify that after logout the poll doesn't loop 401s spamming console (already saw two 401 errors after logout in this test run, low priority).

Rotate-code endpoint has no confirmation flag; the confirm-rotate-btn is UI-only. A malicious script with a valid owner session can call POST /api/team/rotate-code and kick every teammate. Consider requiring `{confirm: true}`.

publish-all payload from members is captured verbatim in approvals.payload — but owner doesn't see the caption/assetId in the current UI approval row (only the truncated summary). Owner should be able to inspect what they're approving. This is a governance risk.
Team.js copy-code-btn doesn't handle clipboard rejection (repeated here — dev-mode uncaught error).

context_for_next_testing_agent: 1) backend_test.py `s` fixture now attaches Authorization: Bearer tok_owner_e2e — if that token gets deleted (e.g. by a logout test), re-seed via `mongosh --eval "use('test_database'); db.user_sessions.insertOne({user_id:'test-owner-1', session_token:'tok_owner_e2e', expires_at:new Date(Date.now()+30*86400e3).toISOString(), created_at:new Date().toISOString()})"`. 2) test_auth_and_approvals.py imports pymongo; installed globally. 3) Run: `pytest backend/tests/ -v --tb=short --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_all.xml`. Expected: 82/82 passing in ~35s. 4) The access code rotates during tests — do NOT hardcode it; always fetch from `GET /api/team` with owner auth. 5) Frontend regression covers all 4 modules end-to-end via owner cookie; the auth-cookie approach works fine for browser tests. 6) UI copy-code-btn triggers clipboard uncaught error overlay in headless — avoid clicking it in future test runs OR grant clipboard permission via `context.grant_permissions(['clipboard-write','clipboard-read'])` before nav.
rca of the issue: No functional bugs — everything asked in the review request works. The one minor discovery (copy-code-btn uncaught clipboard rejection) has a clear fix (try/catch + execCommand fallback). Environment rebuild after corruption is verified clean: every previously-green endpoint still returns 200 (with owner auth), the DB re-seeded correctly (brand=Nonna's Corner Deli, 3 demo baseline weeks in executioner/reports, brand-profile intact, calendar has 2 weeks with real event tiles, maximizer segments/games/spin/qr all healthy). Auth model is deny-by-default with a small OPEN_PATHS set — correct. Approval workflow implementation is correct: members hit submit_or_execute which forks (owner=execute-direct / member=queue-pending); approver.execute reuses the same EXECUTOR registry so member+approve is guaranteed to produce the same result as owner-direct. Rotate-code correctly bumps code_version so `_needs_code` immediately locks out anyone whose stored code_version is stale.
